Terminal maximalist

TUIs you can open anywhere: lazygit, yazi and VisiData

The problem it solves

Three jobs eat a surprising amount of time: remembering the right git command, hunting for a file in a deep folder tree, and finding out what is actually inside a data file before writing a line of code. Typed commands are precise but you cannot see the state, and graphical apps show the state but are slow to drive and do not work over SSH. And I want the same tools on every device I touch: the laptop, the iPad and the phone.

The general idea

A terminal user interface (TUI) sits in between: it shows the whole picture on one screen and you act on it with a couple of keys. They are fast, keyboard-first and they can be extended. And because a TUI only needs a terminal, you can open it basically anywhere: it runs on the machine that has the code and the data, and any device with an SSH client shows it. On my laptop it is a terminal window, on the iPad and the phone it is Blink connected to the computer at home. The apps look and behave the same everywhere. Three carry most of my daily work.

Examples

  • lazygit shows files, branches, commits and the stash together. Staging single hunks or lines, amending a commit, cherry-picking or resolving a conflict takes a few keys instead of a long command. It also opens inside Neovim through a plugin, so I commit without leaving the editor.
  • yazi is a fast file manager with previews for almost everything: images, PDFs, archives, tables. Move with j/k, go in with l, and the preview of the hovered file is always there.
  • VisiData opens CSV, Parquet, JSON, SQLite and many other formats as a sheet and handles millions of rows without complaint. Shift-F turns a column into a frequency table and Shift-I describes the whole sheet with summary statistics. It is the fastest way I know to answer "what is actually in this file?".

Tips from my setup

  • The same three apps on every device. From the iPad or the phone I connect to the computer at home and type lazygit, yazi or vd prices.parquet. I can commit a fix from the sofa, find a file on the train or check a dataset between two talks, with no app to install except a terminal.
  • Clipboard over tmux. I point lazygit's clipboard commands at tmux, so copying works the same over SSH, which matters when I work on a remote machine.
  • yazi plugins for data work. Enter on a .duckdb file opens it in the DuckDB shell while directories and other files behave as usual, one key diffs the selected file with the hovered one, and a space menu holds my custom tools and quick archive and extract commands.
  • VisiData extensions of my own for the questions I keep asking: association heatmaps across all columns (Pearson r for numeric pairs, Cramér's V for categorical ones, variance explained η² for mixed pairs), OLS regression, a decision tree on the current sheet, deduplication, binning, automatic column typing and terminal charts with plotext. VisiData is written in Python, so adding a command is a small function.
